# HydraCache Command Reference

This is the exhaustive, honest list of what HydraCache's TCP (RESP) listener
actually does when a client sends it a command — not what a generic
"Redis-compatible" cache might be expected to support. It's generated by
reading `internal/network/handler.go` and `internal/protocol/commands.go`
directly, not from memory of what Redis does.

Every command below is one of:

- **IMPLEMENTED** — behaves as documented, covered by tests that exercise
  it over a real TCP connection or through the handler directly.
- **PARTIAL** — implemented, but with a stated, deliberate scope boundary.
- **NOT IMPLEMENTED** — returns an error. Where the error message explains
  *why* (rather than a bare "unknown command"), that's noted.

## Wire protocol

HydraCache speaks **RESP2 only**. `HELLO` negotiates protocol version like
real Redis, but requesting protocol 3 gets an honest `NOPROTO` refusal
instead of a silent downgrade or a broken RESP3 encoding — this server does
not implement RESP3's distinct types (map, set, double, boolean, big
number, verbatim string, push, attribute, or the `_\r\n` null). Every reply
below is a RESP2 simple string, error, integer, bulk string, or array.

Errors always start with an uppercase error-code word followed by a space
(`ERR`, `NOAUTH`, `NOPERM`, `WRONGPASS`, `NOPROTO`), matching real Redis
convention, so client libraries that branch on that prefix behave
correctly against HydraCache too.

## Data commands

| Command | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `PING [message]` | IMPLEMENTED | |
| `SET key value [EX seconds \| PX ms] [NX \| XX]` | IMPLEMENTED | `NX` and `XX` together always return nil, matching Redis. `KEEPTTL`, `GET`, and `EXAT`/`PXAT` are not implemented. |
| `SETNX key value` | IMPLEMENTED | The classic two-argument form (distinct from `SET key value NX`) go-redis's `SetNX` client method actually sends on the wire. Found missing by the go-redis compatibility suite before being added. |
| `GET key` | IMPLEMENTED | If the key was migrated to another node by a recent rebalance, the read is transparently forwarded there instead of reporting a false miss. |
| `DEL key [key ...]` | IMPLEMENTED | |
| `EXISTS key [key ...]` | IMPLEMENTED | |
| `TTL key` | IMPLEMENTED | |
| `PTTL key` | IMPLEMENTED | |
| `EXPIRE key seconds` | IMPLEMENTED | No `NX`/`XX`/`GT`/`LT` flags (Redis 7.0+). |
| `PERSIST key` | IMPLEMENTED | |
| `KEYS pattern` | IMPLEMENTED | Only `*` (match all) and plain substring matching — not full glob syntax (`?`, `[abc]`). Like real Redis, this is an O(n) full scan; avoid it against a large keyspace in production. |
| `DBSIZE` | IMPLEMENTED | |
| `FLUSHALL` | IMPLEMENTED | Not replicated as a broadcast to every shard — see the note in `handler.go`'s `replicateWrite`. |
| `INFO [section]` | PARTIAL | Returns a fixed `keys/hits/misses/hit_rate` block; the `section` argument is accepted but ignored (real Redis's many `INFO` sections — `server`, `clients`, `memory`, `replication`, `persistence`, ... — are not implemented). |

## Connection commands

| Command | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH password` / `AUTH username password` | IMPLEMENTED | Returns the real Redis "Client sent AUTH, but no password is set" error when no ACL is configured, rather than "unknown command". |
| `HELLO [2 \| 3] [AUTH user pass] [SETNAME name]` | PARTIAL | Protocol version 2 (or omitted) negotiates normally, including the inline `AUTH` clause go-redis and other modern clients send by default. Version 3 is refused with `NOPROTO` — see "Wire protocol" above. |
| `CLIENT GETNAME` / `CLIENT SETNAME name` | IMPLEMENTED | |
| `CLIENT ID` | IMPLEMENTED | Returns this connection's server-assigned ID (the same value logged as `conn_id` in structured server logs). |
| `CLIENT INFO` | PARTIAL | Returns `id`, `addr`, `name`, `lib-name`, `lib-ver`, `resp` only — not the full field set real Redis reports (`fd`, `age`, `idle`, `db`, `multi`, `watch`, memory usage, and more). |
| `CLIENT SETINFO lib-name\|lib-ver value` | IMPLEMENTED | Accepted and stored so `CLIENT INFO` can report it; go-redis and other modern clients send this unconditionally on connect. |
| `CLIENT LIST` / `KILL` / `PAUSE` / `UNPAUSE` / `NO-EVICT` / `NO-TOUCH` / `REPLY` | NOT IMPLEMENTED | Returns an explicit unknown-subcommand error rather than a fabricated no-op — there is no per-connection registry or eviction-exemption mechanism backing any of these yet. |

## Cluster introspection

| Command | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CLUSTER INFO` | IMPLEMENTED | HydraCache-specific fields (`hydracache_sharded`, `hydracache_node_id`, `hydracache_known_nodes`), not the full real-Redis-Cluster field set. `cluster_enabled` is always `0` — see below. |
| `CLUSTER MYID` | IMPLEMENTED | Returns this node's internal node ID (not a real Redis Cluster 40-character ID). |
| `CLUSTER NODES` / `SLOTS` / `SHARDS` / anything else | NOT IMPLEMENTED (by design) | HydraCache shards via consistent hashing and routes every key server-side; it does **not** speak the Redis Cluster wire protocol (no CRC16 slot assignment, no `MOVED`/`ASK` redirects). Implementing `CLUSTER SLOTS` in Redis Cluster's own format would tell a cluster-aware client it can compute slots and route directly to nodes itself, which would silently misroute since HydraCache's hashing algorithm isn't CRC16-mod-16384. The command is refused with an explanation instead of a fabricated reply. |

## Not exposed over this protocol at all

| Command family | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `PUBLISH` / `SUBSCRIBE` / `PSUBSCRIBE` / ... | NOT IMPLEMENTED | `internal/pubsub` contains a working, tested in-process broker, but nothing in `internal/network` wires it to a client connection. There is no `PUBLISH`/`SUBSCRIBE` command at all right now — sending one gets "unknown command". |
| `MULTI` / `EXEC` / `DISCARD` / `WATCH` | NOT IMPLEMENTED | No transaction support. |
| `SCAN` / `HSCAN` / etc. | NOT IMPLEMENTED | Only `KEYS` (full scan) exists. |
| Hash / List / Set / Sorted-Set data types (`HSET`, `LPUSH`, `SADD`, `ZADD`, ...) | NOT IMPLEMENTED | HydraCache is a string-value cache; there is no secondary data-type support. |
| `SCRIPT` / `EVAL` | NOT IMPLEMENTED | No Lua scripting. |
| `COMMAND` / `COMMAND DOCS` / `COMMAND COUNT` | NOT IMPLEMENTED | Client introspection tooling that calls this on connect (some interactive shells) will get "unknown command" and should treat it as non-fatal, the same way it already tolerates other optional startup commands failing. |

## Inter-node commands

`GOSSIP`, `REPLICATE`, `REPLICA_SYNC`, `ELECTION_VOTE`, `ELECTION_HEARTBEAT`
are real, load-bearing RPCs between HydraCache nodes, not part of the
client-facing surface. They're exempt from AUTH/ACL entirely (see
`isInterNodeCommand` in `handler.go`) since a peer node never authenticates
as a client — node-to-node trust is (or will be) TLS's job, not the
per-connection client session gate. A normal client should never send
these directly.

## Compatibility testing

`internal/network/goredis_compat_test.go` drives a real HydraCache server
with the actual `go-redis/v9` client library — not HydraCache's own
hand-rolled test client — covering `PING`, `SET`/`GET` (including `EX`/
`NX`/`XX`), `DEL`, `EXISTS`, `TTL`, `EXPIRE`, error handling for unknown
commands and wrong arity, and `HELLO`'s negotiation-then-fallback path.
That test is the actual evidence behind the "IMPLEMENTED" markings above
for the commands it covers; everything else in this document is a direct
reading of the dispatch code, not an assumption about it.
